review.translation: [Then|0] [Yahweh|1] [God|2] [built|0] [the rib|4,3] [which|5] [he had taken|6] [from|7] [the man|8] [into a woman|9], [and he brought her|10] [to|11] [the man|12].

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject. אֶת־הַצֵּלָע marks the rib taken from the man as the direct object, and לְאִשָּׁה gives the result. God fashioned the rib into a woman.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ־ precedes יִּבֶן, the shortened third-person masculine singular Qal wayyiqtol of בָּנָה.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּבֶן יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, יַהְוֶה names the subject of וַיִּבֶן ‘he built’, and אֱלֹהִים ‘God’ stands in apposition. Yahweh God builds the rib into a woman.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. The masculine singular verb וַיִּבֶן (“he built”) presents יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים as the one who built the rib into a woman.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular reference and no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הַצֵּלָע ‘the rib’ as the definite direct object of וַיִּבֶן ‘he built’. The rib is what Yahweh God formed into a woman.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הַצֵּלָע as the object of וַיִּבֶן. The clause אֲשֶׁר לָקַח מִן הָאָדָם identifies it as the rib God took from the man and formed into a woman.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a common noun, singular absolute, of common gender.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause לָקַח מִן הָאָדָם, “he took from the man.” Its antecedent is הַצֵּלָע, “the rib,” understood as the object of לָקַח.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In הַצֵּלָע אֲשֶׁר לָקַח מִן הָאָדָם, the rib is what God had taken, and מִן הָאָדָם identifies the man from whom he removed it.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר לָקַח מִן הָאָדָם, “which he took from the man,” מִן identifies the man as the source of the rib.
analysis.morphology: Independent Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: out of, made from; from (a source or giver)

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר לָקַח מִן הָאָדָם, “which he took from the man,” מִן marks the man as the source of the rib. The definite article identifies the particular man already introduced in the narrative.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state with the prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: הַצֵּלָע is the object of וַיִּבֶן, and לְאִשָּׁה identifies what God made the rib into. The feminine singular suffix in וַיְבִאֶהָ then refers to the woman he brought to the man.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ marking the result of וַיִּבֶן, followed by a feminine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים remains the subject. The suffix ־הָ refers to the woman just mentioned in לְאִשָּׁה, and אֶל הָאָדָם identifies the man as the one to whom God brought her.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and a third feminine singular object suffix ־הָ.
analysis.sense: bring someone or something to a destination

analysis.evidence: In וַיְבִאֶהָ אֶל הָאָדָם, “he brought her to the man,” the suffix on וַיְבִאֶהָ identifies the woman as the one brought. אֶל marks הָאָדָם as the goal of that movement.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: to a person as the goal of movement

analysis.evidence: In וַיְבִאֶהָ אֶל הָאָדָם (“he brought her to the man”), הָאָדָם identifies the same man from whom God took the rib earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed definite article הָ־.
